title: Status-for-sovereignty compact and the white-dominant selector state
working_proposition: A vertically stratified coalition can exchange mass status restoration for expanded executive and founder-capital sovereignty: grievance and nested superiority legitimate the subordination of independent counterpower; public authority then controls selection, capital, procurement, infrastructure, and institutional succession; conditional multiracial incorporation legitimates the selector; and counterfactual foreclosure makes the preferred order appear meritocratic without requiring a central conspiracy or uniform private intent.
negative_constitution: No outside actor may convert contradiction, patterned outcome, affected-party evidence, or an alternative into a binding pause, correction, substitution, or value claim unless the protected center admits the challenge on terms the center controls.

racial_order_hypothesis.label: white_dominant_conditionally_multiracial
racial_order_hypothesis.definition: An institutional order may remain white-dominant when rules, burdens, classifications, defaults, remedies, and status allocations preserve a racial hierarchy while permitting sincere and sometimes powerful non-White incorporation on terms that validate the selector and do not create independent collective counterpower.
must_test: public contribution and private residual rights
racial_order_hypothesis.forbidden_shortcut: Demography, rhetoric, disparity, or individual success alone establishes the racial order.

patriotism_discriminator.question: When does patriotism or national-security language express ordinary collective purpose, and when does it legitimate a status hierarchy, narrow admissible knowledge, remove counterpower, or convert public authority into protected private control?

patriotism_discriminator.forbidden_inference: Patriotic or national-security rhetoric alone proves white supremacy, fascism, coordination, or coercive operation.

field_sources.title: Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programs and Preferencing
normalized_fact_record: Orders federal agencies to terminate DEI, DEIA, environmental-justice offices, positions, plans, grants, contracts, and performance requirements to the maximum extent allowed by law.
Frames the targeted programs as illegal, immoral, discriminatory, wasteful, and inconsistent with equal dignity, merit, and making America great.
Directs review and revision of federal employment practices, union contracts, and training policies.
limitations: Does not establish the legality, effectiveness, or racial effect of each terminated program.
Does not establish implementation across every agency.
Does not establish a white-dominant order or common purpose.

field_sources.title: Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity
normalized_fact_record: Revokes Executive Order 11246 and directs OFCCP to cease promoting diversity, affirmative action, and workforce balancing.
Requires federal contracts and grants to include anti-discrimination compliance terms and certifications regarding unlawful DEI programs.
Directs agencies to identify sectors, entities, investigations, litigation, and regulatory action concerning allegedly illegal DEI preferences.
limitations: Does not establish that all DEI programs are unlawful.
Does not provide the complete affected-contractor denominator or later enforcement outcomes.
Does not establish racial intent or a complete SSC chain.

field_sources.title: Restoring Equality of Opportunity and Meritocracy
normalized_fact_record: Executive Order 14281 declares a policy to eliminate disparate-impact liability to the maximum degree possible.
Directs agencies to deprioritize enforcement of statutes and regulations to the extent they include disparate-impact liability.
Directs the Attorney General to initiate repeal or amendment of Title VI regulations contemplating disparate-impact liability and review pending matters.
limitations: Does not eliminate every statutory disparate-impact cause of action by itself.
Does not establish the practical effect on any specific affected population.
Does not establish that patterned outcomes are irrelevant or that racial hierarchy follows.

field_sources.title: Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors
normalized_fact_record: Executive Order 14398 requires covered federal contracts to contain a clause prohibiting racially discriminatory DEI activities by contractors and subcontractors.
Authorizes cancellation, termination, or suspension of contracts and suspension or debarment for noncompliance.
Requires information access, subcontractor reporting, OMB guidance, sector-risk identification, and FAR implementation.
limitations: Does not establish the number of affected contractors or actual enforcement actions.
Does not establish that lawful equal-opportunity programs are prohibited.
Does not establish racial animus or prevalence.

field_sources.title: Removing Discrimination and Discriminatory Equity Ideology From the Foreign Service
normalized_fact_record: Directs revision of Foreign Service tenure and promotion criteria to remove the DEIA Core Precept.
Directs officials not to base Foreign Service recruitment, hiring, promotion, or retention on protected characteristics.
Directs review of members alleged to have knowingly and willfully engaged in unconstitutional or illegal discrimination and authorizes appropriate personnel action.
limitations: Does not establish how many decisions changed or whether merit criteria improved.
Does not establish any specific member committed unlawful discrimination.
Does not establish racial hierarchy or a complete correction record.

field_sources.title: Ames v. Ohio Department of Youth Services, slip opinion
field_sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
normalized_fact_record: The unanimous Court held that the Sixth Circuit background-circumstances rule imposed an impermissible heightened evidentiary burden on majority-group Title VII plaintiffs.
The Court vacated the judgment and remanded for application of the proper prima facie standard.
The opinion states that Title VII draws no distinction between majority-group and minority-group plaintiffs for disparate-treatment proof.
limitations: Does not resolve Ames merits or prove discrimination.
Does not validate every anti-DEI policy.
Does not establish a national racial-order finding.

field_sources.title: Docket 23-1039, Ames v. Ohio Department of Youth Services
field_sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
normalized_fact_record: Records grant, argument, unanimous June 5 2025 decision, vacatur, remand, and July 7 judgment issuance.
Preserves the procedural history and parties for the opinion used in SSC-OBS-0006.
limitations: Docket metadata does not substitute for the opinion holding.
Does not establish merits on remand.

field_sources.title: 2026 NatSec100 methodology
normalized_fact_record: Uses a proprietary weighted scoring system developed with Pryzm, Balyasny Asset Management, and Franklin Templeton.
Inputs include government contracting activity, recent and total capital raised, and recent headcount growth.
Eligibility requires venture or private-equity backing, defense applicability, at least one U.S. government contract by December 31 2025, and FOCI vetting.
Acknowledges public-data, classified-work, valuation, and operational-impact limitations.
limitations: Does not disclose full weights, candidate denominator, rejected companies, or all vetting decisions.
Ranking inclusion does not prove procurement influence or technical superiority.
First-party methodology is not independent validation.

field_sources.title: First 18 SBIC Critical Technologies Initiative funds
normalized_fact_record: DoD and SBA published the entire first cohort of 18 licensed or Green Light approved funds, with one fund name withheld under SBA policy.
The cohort was projected to invest more than $4 billion across more than 1,700 companies and multiple investment stages.
Approval required an application, operational and investment due diligence, legal review, formal interview, and committee approvals.
Seven funds were fully licensed and had commenced investment activity.
limitations: Does not disclose the complete applicant and rejection denominator.
Projected investment is not realized deployment or public benefit.
Fund approval does not prove coordination or favoritism.

field_sources.title: OSC receives $8.9 billion in financing requests
normalized_fact_record: OSC received more than 200 applications totaling $8.9 billion for an inaugural manufacturing loan program.
The requests exceeded the program current lending capacity of $984 million.
Requests ranged from $10 million to $150 million across 38 states and multiple critical-technology sectors.
At publication OSC was reviewing applications and expected later selections.
limitations: Does not identify all applicants or later selections.
Demand does not establish program effectiveness or capture.
No complete rights, performance, or recovery record is supplied.

field_sources.title: OSC first direct loan to MP Materials
normalized_fact_record: OSC announced a $150 million direct loan to add heavy rare-earth separation capacity at MP Materials Mountain Pass facility.
The loan was part of a wider July 2025 DoD agreement and funded through statutory credit subsidy.
The enabling law provided $500 million in credit subsidy described as supporting up to $100 billion in critical-minerals loans.
limitations: Does not publish the complete loan agreement, pricing, security, covenants, or recovery history.
Does not establish favoritism or extraction.
Does not establish final performance.

field_sources.title: DoD awards $14.3 million to Anduril for solid rocket motors
normalized_fact_record: DoD announced a $14.3 million DPA Title III award to Anduril to expand solid-rocket-motor production.
The release states the award builds on Anduril private capital investment of $75 million.
The funding supports facility modification, manufacturing-process improvement, testing, quality assurance, and final assembly in Mississippi.
limitations: Does not disclose the full applicant or alternative-supplier denominator.
Does not disclose complete award terms or public recovery rights.
Does not prove Anduril was intrinsically superior or part of a common-purpose organism.

field_sources.title: Anduril additional $43.7 million DPA funding statement
normalized_fact_record: Anduril states it received $43.7 million in additional DPA Title III funding on October 2 2025.
The statement connects the funding to expanded testing, storage, tooling, production capacity, allied sales, and supplier selection.
The statement frames public-private support and Anduril emergence as evidence of industrial-base success.
limitations: First-party statement does not supply the award instrument, applicant denominator, full public rights, or independent performance evaluation.
Public funding plus company success does not establish merit circularity.
Does not establish private extraction or common purpose.

field_sources.title: Polar Semiconductor CHIPS Incentives award
normalized_fact_record: Commerce finalized up to $123 million in direct CHIPS funding for Polar Semiconductor after due diligence.
Disbursement is tied to completion of project components, production, and commercial milestones.
The project represented more than $525 million from private, state, and federal sources and was expected to nearly double capacity.
The release describes compliance monitoring and a majority-U.S.-ownership transition.
limitations: Does not supply the full applicant denominator or award agreement.
Projected jobs and capacity are not final observed outcomes.
Does not establish neutrality of every industrial-policy program.

field_sources.title: VMD Systems Integrators bid protest decision
normalized_fact_record: GAO sustained VMD protests after finding FEMA used unstated evaluation criteria and did not refute an awardee labor-category allegation.
GAO recommended reevaluation or solicitation amendment, a new selection if warranted, and reimbursement of protest costs.
The decision provides an observed independent correction route inside federal procurement.
limitations: Does not establish final agency implementation or award outcome.
One sustained protest does not prove procurement generally contestable.
Does not establish any racial-order proposition.

field_sources.title: The trainwreck is a vertical coalition, not a flat one
normalized_fact_record: Names a status-for-sovereignty compact organized as a vertical coalition with nested superiority.
Proposes conditional multiracial incorporation, allocator transfer, preference monopoly, counterfactual foreclosure, and distributed counterpower aversion.
Defines Question 4 as the practical test of standing, evidence, pause, correction, substitution, exit, and value recovery.
limitations: Structural synthesis and field hypothesis, not an independently verified empirical denominator.
Cannot establish the secret intent of voters, founders, investors, officials, or institutions.
Original attachment bytes are not preserved; the repository stores a bounded transcription.

field_sources.title: The Symbolic Politics of Status in the MAGA Movement
field_sources.publisher: Perspectives on Politics, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Analyzes MAGA as a status movement centered on lost honor, declining esteem, and perceived institutional disrespect.
Records belonging, pride, anger, and joy alongside grievance and policy preference.
Supplies a bounded status-motive mechanism rather than a national electorate denominator.
limitations: Ethnography does not establish every supporter’s motive.
No exact gate or consequence chain is supplied.
Status grievance alone does not establish racial hierarchy.

field_sources.title: Embracing the Status Hierarchy: How Immigration Attitudes, Prejudice, and Sexism Shaped Non-White Support for Trump
field_sources.publisher: Perspectives on Politics, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Across multiple datasets, hierarchy-related attitudes are associated with Trump support among Black, Latino, and Asian respondents.
Hierarchy-supporting attitudes are not unique to White respondents.
The association supports coalition heterogeneity without establishing individual motive or institutional order.
limitations: Associations do not establish every voter’s motive.
No institutional selection and remedy denominator is supplied.
Non-White support proves neither neutrality nor tokenism.

field_sources.title: Detailed demographic profiles of Trump and Harris voters in 2024
normalized_fact_record: Pew reports that 78 percent of Trump’s 2024 voters were non-Hispanic White.
About one-fifth of Trump’s 2024 coalition was Hispanic, Black, Asian, or another race.
Composition establishes a genuinely multiracial coalition but not its governing structure or effects.
limitations: Composition cannot identify individual motive.
Diversity does not establish neutrality or justice.
No exact selector, consequence, or remedy is identified.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: 2026 NatSec100 report and methodology
normalized_fact_record: Publishes a complete selected roster of 100 ranked companies for the 2026 edition.
Uses a proprietary weighted model with U.S. government contracting activity, recent capital raised, total capital raised, and recent headcount growth as disclosed inputs.

Requires venture or private-equity backing, no public listing or filed IPO, no acquisition by a public company, public defense or dual-use applicability, at least one U.S. government contract by December 31 2025, and FOCI vetting.
Explains SpaceX exclusion under the IPO rule and describes Anthropic as formally evaluated but ineligible at publication during an active contract dispute and litigation.
States that signals are not outcomes and acknowledges public-data, classified-work, valuation, and operational-impact limits.
limitations: Does not disclose the complete candidate universe, exact weights, rejected-company rows, or FOCI decisions.
Ranking inclusion does not prove technical superiority, procurement causation, investment causation, or common purpose.
The published roster is a first-party selected denominator, not an independently reproduced candidate denominator.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: SBA and DoD celebrate first year of SBICCT
normalized_fact_record: Reports 22 formal SBICCT applications since launch and 13 funds approved for Green Light or licensing as of October 22 2024.
States that 12 firms managed the 13 funds and planned $2.8 billion in private capital matched with SBA-guaranteed loans.
States that licensees could access up to $175 million in SBA-guaranteed leverage and program-related DoD benefits.
limitations: Does not name all 22 applicants or the nine applications not in the 13-fund approved group.
Does not disclose applicant scoring, per-fund leverage commitments, realized returns, failures, or recovery.
The October 2024 denominator is time-bounded and does not describe later cohorts.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: First 18 SBIC Critical Technologies Initiative funds
normalized_fact_record: Declares the entire first cohort to contain 18 Licensed or Green Light Approved funds.
States that 17 fund names are shown in the official graphic and one Green Light fund withheld its name under SBA policy.
States that seven funds were fully licensed and had begun investing.
Reports more than 100 funds had expressed interest and that diligence had begun on a second cohort.
Projects more than $4 billion of investment across more than 1,700 portfolio companies.
limitations: Does not disclose the complete applicant and rejection denominator for the first or second cohort.
The 17 names are presented in a graphic and are not separately transcribed in this supplement.
Projections are not realized deployment, returns, public benefit, or repayment.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: SBICCT Investment Policy Statement
normalized_fact_record: Defines the joint SBA and DoD portfolio objectives and governance framework for SBICCT.
Covers strategic sectors, stages, asset allocation, portfolio construction, licensee management, risk management, monitoring, and reporting.
Records that the initiative began accepting SBIC licensure applications on September 29 2023.
limitations: Portfolio-level governance does not disclose per-fund selection scores, leverage commitments, returns, failures, or recovery.
Policy rules do not establish how every selected fund performed.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: Manage an SBIC: leverage and repayment terms
normalized_fact_record: Describes standard-debenture leverage as typically no more than two times private capital, with a ten-year term and stated fees.
Describes accrual-debenture leverage and repayment obligations tied to distributions to private investors.
Requires leverage proceeds to be used for qualifying small-business investments.
limitations: These are general SBIC terms and do not establish the exact instrument or commitment for any SBICCT fund.
General repayment priority does not establish realized public recovery or fund performance.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: 89 FR 79271: OSC equipment-finance Notice of Funding Availability
targeted_acquisition_sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register / Department of Defense
normalized_fact_record: Makes up to $984 million available for direct equipment-finance loans in 31 covered technology categories.
Sets expected loan sizes from $10 million to $150 million and anticipates approximately ten successful applicants.
Uses a two-stage process and identifies statutory compliance, national or economic security impact, project additionality, and creditworthiness among selection criteria.
limitations: Does not identify applicants, invitees to the second stage, selected or rejected rows, or negotiated loan terms.
The planned approximate award count is not the observed final denominator.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC receives $8.9 billion in manufacturing financing requests
normalized_fact_record: Reports more than 200 applications totaling $8.9 billion against $984 million in current lending capacity.
Reports applicants from 38 states across sizes, stages, and sectors, with requests from $10 million to $150 million.
States that applications were under review and selected applicants were expected later in 2025.
limitations: Does not identify applicants, selection scores, second-stage invitees, selected or rejected rows, or terms.
Application demand does not establish favoritism, capture, effectiveness, or complete public benefit.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC Credit Program current status
normalized_fact_record: States that the September 27 2024 equipment-finance Part 1 window closed on February 3 2025.
States that OSC continues to engage directly with existing applicants and is no longer accepting Part 1 submissions for the first NOFA.
Describes direct debt financing for eligible borrowers in critical technology areas.
limitations: Does not publish the applicant roster, second-stage invitees, award denominator, rejected rows, or complete agreements.
A current program-status page does not prove disbursement, milestones, defaults, or recovery.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC first direct loan to MP Materials
normalized_fact_record: Reports execution of a $150 million direct loan to MP Materials for heavy rare-earth separation capacity at Mountain Pass, California.
Identifies the transaction as OSC’s first direct loan and links it to July 2025 legislation providing credit-subsidy funding.
Names the borrower, amount, facility, and intended use.
limitations: Does not publish the complete loan agreement, pricing, security, covenants, disbursement schedule, performance, defaults, or recovery history.
Does not establish that MP Materials was selected from the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC conditional commitments to Vulcan Elements and ReElement Technologies
normalized_fact_record: Reports separate conditional loan commitments of $620 million to Vulcan Elements and $80 million to ReElement Technologies.
States that the Department will receive warrants from both companies and that Commerce proposed incentives and equity for Vulcan.
States that no OSC funds are disbursed until financial, legal, technical, and other conditions are completed.
limitations: Conditional commitments are not executed loans or disbursements.
Does not publish the complete agreements, warrant terms, valuation, milestones, defaults, or recovery.
Does not establish that either company was selected from the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC conditional commitment to Phoenix Tailings
normalized_fact_record: Reports a $500 million conditional loan commitment to Phoenix Tailings for domestic rare-earth processing.
States that OSC financing plus additional private capital are intended to provide approximately $1 billion.
States that financial, legal, technical, and other due diligence remains before financial close.
limitations: Conditional commitment is not an executed loan or disbursement.
Does not publish the complete agreement, private-capital denominator, milestones, defaults, or recovery.
Does not establish relation to the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

targeted_acquisition_sources.title: OSC conditional commitment to Energy Fuels
normalized_fact_record: Reports a $725 million conditional loan commitment to Energy Fuels for domestic rare-earth processing.
States that financial, legal, technical, and other due diligence remains before financial close.
Reports that OSC had committed more than $5 billion in FY26 debt financing and mobilized more than $11 billion in total public and private capital.
limitations: Conditional commitment is not an executed loan or disbursement.
The named transactions in this supplement do not exhaust the reported FY26 aggregate.
Does not publish the complete agreement, milestones, defaults, recovery, or relation to the first NOFA applicant universe.
